title: Finite-ring vector-bundle orientation restricted to the zero section
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $N\geq1$ with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be Noetherian with $N$ invertible on $S$. Work in the ordinary unbounded categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves, with exact inverse images. For every compactifiable structural map $b$ write $\omega_b=b^\times A$ using the right adjoint of $Rb_!$. Put $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$ and $A_T(d)=A_T(1)^{\otimes d}$, with $A_T(0)=A_T$.
Let $\pi:E\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$, with zero section $z$. Assume $\pi$ is compactifiable. For every affine trivializing open $T\subseteq S$ and linear frame $\phi:E_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf A^d_T$ over $T$, let
$$o_\phi:z_T^*\omega_{\pi_T}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(d)[2d]$$
be the section restriction of the inverse of the adjoint $\alpha_{p_d}:A_{\mathbf A^d_T}(d)[2d]\to\omega_{p_d}$ of the Kummer-normalized coordinate-tower counit, transported through $\phi$ by the counit-preserving comparison of compact-support right adjoints. For every overlap and every invertible linear change of frames these $o_\phi$ agree under the canonical restriction maps. They glue to a unique isomorphism
$$o_E:z^*\omega_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}A_S(d)[2d]$$
with these frame restrictions. It is preserved by every $S$-linear bundle isomorphism, using the counit-preserving comparison on the source. For $d=0$, $o_E$ is the identity under $E\cong S$. Empty bases and $A=0$ are allowed.
If $A=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$, $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\geq1$, and $\ell$ is invertible on $S$, let $\gamma_{\pi,A_S}:A_E(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi^\times A_S$ be the purity map adjoint to vector-bundle integration and the canonical projection formula. Then
$$o_E=z^*(\gamma_{\pi,A_S}^{-1})$$
under the canonical ordinary-etale Tate coefficient identifications.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-sbc-affine-space], [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], [def-amb-vector-integration].

source.place: Orientation-charts proof Step 4, linear normalization and comparison to bundle purity; old item Step 16.

proof.text: Check the geometric hypotheses on the objects used below. The projective completion of [lem-amb-vector-projective-completion] gives Noetherian total and compactification spaces for every bundle over a Noetherian base, including the trivial bundle. The open-subscheme lemma makes every trivializing open and every intersection of such opens Noetherian. Thus all the compact-support functors and right adjoints below are defined. For every affine open in its target, the inverse image under an open immersion is an open in a Noetherian scheme, hence quasi-compact by the same lemma. Each open immersion in question is therefore quasi-compact and is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Its diagonal identifies with the identity of its source, so is closed: the immersion is separated. Isomorphisms are open immersions onto the whole target and satisfy the same hypotheses. Thus the open adjunctions and composition comparisons apply. Invertibility of $N$ restricts to these opens, and $A$ remains finite with $NA=0$. Write $L_X=A_X(d)[2d]$; the Tate pullback identifications identify this object under each map of schemes used below.

source.place: Step 4, hypotheses for vector-bundle integration and linear changes of frame

proof.text: For an affine-space projection $p=p_{d,T}$, use the actual coordinate-tower adjunction $F_d\dashv G_d$ in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], with $G_d=p^*(-)(d)[2d]$. The unbounded compact-support composition comparisons identify its left functor $F_d$ with $Rp_!$ on the whole ordinary derived category: each affine-line factor is the chosen proper/open compactification functor, and the tower compositor is the one of the comparison theorem. Its restriction on $L_X$ is therefore the bounded-below comparison used to define $t_p$. Conjugating this left-functor isomorphism gives a counit-preserving isomorphism $G_d\cong p^\times$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. At $A_T$ its component is exactly the adjunct $\alpha_p:L_X\to p^\times A_T$ of $t_p$, because the defining equation for this conjugate is equality of the counits. Hence $\alpha_p$ is invertible. This uses the affine-space adjunction, rather than inferring invertibility of an adjunct from invertibility of its trace alone.

source.place: Step 4, specified coordinate adjunction and its counit normalization

proof.text:
Make the restriction comparison precise. For an open $u:T\hookrightarrow S$, put $v:E_T\hookrightarrow E$ and $b=\pi_T$. Compose the open adjunctions of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] with compact supports. For every $M\in D(E_T{}_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the resulting natural Hom identifications are
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,v^*\pi^\times A_S)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!M,\pi^\times A_S)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R\pi_!v_!M,A_S)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u_!Rb_!M,A_S)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rb_!M,A_T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,b^\times A_T).$$
The middle identification uses $\pi v=ub$ and the unbounded compact-support compositor. Thus the conjugate comparisons for the two composite adjunctions give the counit-preserving isomorphism $c_u:v^*\omega_\pi\cong\omega_b$. The mate-pasting identities show that these comparisons compose under nested opens and source isomorphisms. In particular, a restricted adjunct is the adjunct of the restricted trace after compact-support exchange. These are the canonical restriction maps in the statement; no unrestricted exceptional base-change assertion is needed.

source.place: Step 4, canonical restriction and counit-preserving source comparison

proof.text:
Apply the preceding Hom calculation to $p_{d,T}$ and an open $W\subseteq T$. The base-change equality for the actual trace in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] says $t_{p_{d,W}}C=u^*t_{p_{d,T}}$, where $C$ is compact-support exchange on $L$. The canonical Tate pullback identification and the Hom calculation therefore give
$$c_u\,v^*\alpha_{p_{d,T}}=\alpha_{p_{d,W}}.$$
Invert and pull back by zero. This proves restriction compatibility of the proposed affine section orientations. The trace equality applies even when $W$ is not affine: it is Noetherian by Step 1, and the affine-space trace theorem permits any Noetherian base. Pasting gives the same equation after transporting through a frame.

source.place: Step 4, restriction of the coordinate adjunction to overlaps

proof.text:
Over a Noetherian overlap $W$, let $a_g$ be an invertible linear substitution and let $\theta_g:a_g^*L\cong L$ be Tate pullback. Let $c_g:a_g^*\omega_p\cong\omega_p$ be the counit-preserving comparison for $pa_g=p$. Under the adjunction $Rp_!\dashv p^\times$, the map $c_g a_g^*\alpha_p\theta_g^{-1}:L\to\omega_p$ has transpose $t_p\rho_g^{-1}$: one moves the pulled-back argument across the isomorphism adjunction, so its compact-support identification is inverse to the pullback action $\rho_g$ specified in [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance]. This is the source-isomorphism case of mate pasting. That lemma gives $t_p\rho_g=t_p$, hence also $t_p\rho_g^{-1}=t_p$. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection yields
$$c_g a_g^*\alpha_p=\alpha_p\theta_g.$$
Since $a_g0=0$, inversion and zero-section pullback identify the two section orientations. By [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], two frames on any overlap differ by exactly such a matrix over $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. Together with Step 4 this proves equality of the prescribed $o_\phi$ on all overlaps, including arbitrary invertible linear changes, without a determinant factor.

source.place: Step 4, linear normalization and preservation by a linear bundle isomorphism

proof.text: Choose an affine trivializing cover $(T_i)$. Put $M=(z^*\omega_\pi)[-2d]$ and $P=A_S(d)[0]$. Exact inverse image and the canonical Tate comparisons identify $M|_{T_i}$ and $P|_{T_i}$ with $A_{T_i}(d)[0]$ by Step 2 and the open comparison of Step 3. Both therefore have cohomology only in degree zero on this cover. Apply [lem-pur-degree-zero-derived-map-gluing] to $M,P$ and the compatible maps $o_{\phi_i}[-2d]$ from Steps 4--5. It supplies a unique global map. Apply the same lemma to their inverses, which agree because the maps do; uniqueness applied to the two composites makes them identity maps. Shifting back gives the isomorphism $o_E$. For a frame not in the chosen cover, compare on its intersections with the $T_i$ and apply the same injectivity statement there. Thus $o_E$ has every prescribed frame restriction and is uniquely determined by them. This glues maps between locally degree-zero objects, not arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Step 4, gluing the frame restrictions; Stacks Tags 06XS, 03EM and 04TQ

proof.text: Let $h:E\xrightarrow{\sim}E'$ be an $S$-linear bundle isomorphism. A frame $\phi'$ on $E'_T$ induces the frame $\phi'h$ on $E_T$, and $h z=z'$. The source-isomorphism adjunction comparison identifies $h^*\omega_{\pi'}$ with $\omega_\pi$ by [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Conjugation and mate pasting make the comparison for $\phi'h$ the composite of those for $h$ and $\phi'$. Hence, after zero-section pullback, the map obtained from $o_{E'}$ by $h$ has local restriction precisely $o_{\phi'h}$. Step 6 makes this map equal to $o_E$. This proves the stated naturality, using the specified counit-preserving source comparison.

At $d=0$ the coordinate tower is the identity adjunction, $A(0)[0]=A$, and its counit and adjunct are identities. The rank-zero symmetric algebra and its augmentation identify $E,z,\pi$ with $S,1_S,1_S$. Thus all frame maps are identities and unique gluing gives $o_E=1$. If $S$ is empty the degree-zero gluing statement includes the empty cover. If $A=0$, every unital $A$-module is zero, so all the displayed objects are zero objects and their unique maps are the asserted isomorphisms. In particular $N=1$ is covered, since $NA=0$ then forces $A=0$.

source.place: Step 4, identity normalization and degenerate cases

proof.text: For the final coefficient comparison, first compute the canonical projection map at $K=A_S$. Under tensor-unit identifications its proper factor is identity: in [def-kun-projection-formula-map] the adjoint defining this factor reduces to the counit $r^*Rr_*L\to L$, whose transpose is $1_{Rr_*L}$ by the triangle identity. The coefficient-first projection map named in [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] is, by [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], this $\mathrm{PF}_r$ conjugated by the derived symmetries $\sigma$ of [lem-kun-tensor-sym]; at the unit $A_S$ in degree zero the sign $(-1)^{pq}$ is $1$ and each symmetry followed by the unitor is the other unitor, so it gives the same map. Its open factor is identity under the unitors as well: the open tensor comparison is induced by $j_!P\otimes A\cong j_!(P\otimes j^*A)$, which sends a local section to itself. Consequently inverse projection followed by $1\otimes t_\pi$ and the unitor, at $K=A_S$, is exactly $t_\pi$. Thus the map called $\gamma_{\pi,A_S}$ in the statement is the adjunct of $t_\pi$, with no residual unit automorphism.

source.place: Step 4, comparison to integration-normalized bundle purity; projection map at the coefficient unit

proof.text: Now take $A=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ and $\ell$ invertible on $S$. The theorem [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] applies on these ordinary unbounded categories to $K=A_S$ and gives the specified invertible $\gamma_{\pi,A_S}$. By [def-amb-vector-integration], $t_\pi$ restricts, through a frame and compact-support exchange, to the very same coordinate-tower counit $t_{p_d}$. Steps 3 and 9 then identify the restriction of $\gamma_{\pi,A_S}$ with $\alpha_{p_d}$. Invert and pull back along $z_T$: the frame restrictions of $z^*(\gamma_{\pi,A_S}^{-1})$ are $o_\phi$. The uniqueness in Step 6 proves the desired equality with $o_E$. The coefficient identifications are exactly those in the bundle-purity theorem. In particular, if its Tate line uses an $\ell$-power annihilator instead of $N$, compare both with a common-multiple annihilator; [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identifies the lines by the roots-of-unity power maps, compatibly with their tensors and inverse images. No field assumption on $A$, flatness over $\mathbf Z/N$, or general smooth-purity theorem enters the argument.

source.place: Step 4, comparison with the inverse vector-bundle purity map
